absent: Full definitions, sizes and ownership of balancing environment, group statistics, domain statistics and runqueue objects.
Locking order, exclusion guarantees and lifetime rules for shared domain storage and cache count tables.
Contracts, side effects and failure modes of capacity, utilization, migration admissibility and sibling imbalance helpers.
Reset policy for balance failure counters and configuration ranges for patience thresholds and NUMA parameters.
Callers, scheduling contexts and frequency expectations for the busiest selection, imbalance planning and active balancing paths.

findings.text: Predicate llc_balance approves cache driven balancing only after several vetoes fail. It stays negative when the cache feature is disabled, when the domain shares a cache, when asymmetric capacity handling must prioritize a misfit load, or when recent failures reach one past the configured patience threshold. Otherwise it approves only when the candidate group reports a nonzero count of tasks preferring the destination cache and the cache migration admissibility check allows movement from the representative processor of that group toward the destination processor.

A build without cache awareness disables the same decisions unconditionally. The group cache statistics recorder does nothing and the cache balancing predicate plus the cache busiest comparator plus the cache veto of active balancing all deny in every case, so no cache driven migration kind can be selected.

When cache awareness is active, the cache busiest comparator prefers a candidate whose count of tasks preferring the destination cache strictly exceeds the current best count, providing a simple majority preference rule for cache locality.

Busiest group selection first discards candidates with no runnable tasks and applies asymmetric capacity vetoes. A misfit candidate is ignored unless the destination core is idle and offers strictly greater capacity than the candidate peak while the local group still has spare, and a lightly loaded candidate with higher minimum capacity than the destination is ignored to protect throughput. Surviving candidates are then ordered by group category rank, with a higher rank always winning and a lower rank always losing without further comparison.

When candidate and current best share the same group category, a category specific metric decides. Groups with spare prefer fewer idle processors and then more running tasks, with an extra rule that avoids pulling the sole task from a shared capacity group when comparing against a non shared group. Fully busy groups prefer higher average load, breaking exact ties against a shared capacity incumbent. Load sharing groups with spare handling reuse the spare rule when either side has idle processors. Misfit groups prefer larger misfit load, packing groups prefer the lower priority processor indicator, cache groups delegate to the cache preference comparator, imbalanced groups keep the first seen, and overloaded groups prefer higher average load.

Locality classification distinguishes queues and groups by how many runnable tasks lack locality. A count exceeding the nonlocal total yields the regular value, otherwise a count exceeding the preferred total yields the remote value, otherwise the result is the universal value. One build variant fixes group classification to the universal value while another build variant fixes queue classification to the regular value, collapsing the three way distinction.

The idle scan hint is maintained only for periodic balancing when the utilization search feature is enabled and shared domain storage exists. It converts total utilization into an average per processor share, applies a downward quadratic curve that reaches zero when utilization attains the overload ratio derived from the domain imbalance percentage, scales the curve back to a processor count, clamps intermediate values to the capacity scale, and publishes the result with a single write only when the rounded count changed.

Imbalance planning assigns a migration kind and amount from the busiest category before considering averages. Misfit handling requests a single misfit move under asymmetric capacity and otherwise requests a load move sized by the misfit load. Packing handling requests as many task moves as runnable tasks in the busiest group. Sharing, cache locality and imbalanced categories each request a single task move, with cache locality using its dedicated migration kind.

When the local group has spare, an overloaded busiest outside a shared cache domain triggers a utilization move sized to fill local headroom, upgraded to a single task move when the local processor is idle but headroom is zero. Otherwise the plan spreads tasks evenly, using sibling aware sizing for single processor busiest groups or sibling preference and otherwise balancing idle processor counts, then applying a NUMA tolerance adjustment and halving the result. When the local side is not yet overloaded its average is compared against busiest and global averages with zero imbalance on no progress, and the fully loaded path requests a load move sized to the smaller of the busiest surplus and the local deficit relative to the global average.

NUMA tolerance suppresses tiny imbalances on lightly loaded destinations. When destination activity exceeds the configured busy threshold the requested amount passes through unchanged, otherwise amounts at or below the minimal imbalance constant collapse to zero while larger amounts pass through.

Source queue search iterates over processors common to the candidate group span and the allowed mask, skipping queues whose locality class exceeds the environment allowance and queues with no runnable fair tasks. Under asymmetric capacity a lone task queue is skipped unless cluster capacity equality or degraded sharing capacity applies or the destination offers strictly greater capacity, and asymmetric priority ordering also skips lone task queues that would violate preferred direction.

Among surviving source candidates the best is chosen by the active migration kind. Load search maximizes load per capacity using cross products and ignores a lone task whose load exceeds the planned imbalance unless the source capacity check passes. Utilization search maximizes boosted fair utilization while ignoring lone task queues. Task count search maximizes runnable count. Misfit search maximizes misfit load. Cache task search maximizes the count of tasks preferring the destination cache as observed through the source domain table when the destination cache index is in range.
Boosted fair utilization is obtained by delegating to the generic processor utilization query with fixed arguments that select boosted accounting.

Active balancing is forced unless a cache veto blocks it. Forcing occurs for asymmetric packing when the destination is idle and priority rules favor movement, for task migration after failures exceed two beyond the cache patience threshold, for an idle destination pulling a lone fair task from a constrained source with sufficient capacity gain, and unconditionally for misfit and cache task migration kinds. Otherwise no active move is requested.

Cache veto of active balancing applies only when caching is enabled and source and destination do not share a cache and every runnable fair task on the source prefers its current cache. Misfit migration never vetoes. Otherwise a lone task source vetoes, and a busier source vetoes when its current fair task misfits asymmetric capacity or when cache migration policy forbids movement at the observed utilization. All other cases allow active balancing to proceed.

Observed balancing state centers on an environment carrying domain, destination and source processors, migration kind, imbalance amount, failure tolerance, locality allowance and idle hints, group statistics carrying runnable counts, locality counts, average load, capacity, utilization, idle processor counts and misfit load, domain statistics carrying local and busiest group snapshots plus totals and sibling preference, and runqueues carrying runnable counts, fair runnable counts, locality counts, misfit load and current task pointer.

Shared balancing data uses lightweight concurrency controls. Asymmetric priority indicators are sampled with single read accessors, the idle scan hint is published with a single write accessor only on change, and runqueue domain tables plus current task pointers are observed through a dereference helper suitable for concurrent reclamation. No explicit sleeping locks appear in the routed fragments.

Stale or torn observations can skew balancing. Priority indicators and scan hints rely on single access ordering rather than full exclusion, domain tables and current task pointers can change concurrently, average and utilization snapshots may race with migration, and scan scaling divides by domain weight which must be nonzero for a defined result.

Balancing uses domain attributes including SD_SHARE_LLC and SD_ASYM_CPUCAPACITY and SD_SHARE_CPUCAPACITY, group categories including group_overloaded and group_llc_balance and group_imbalanced and group_asym_packing and group_misfit_task and group_smt_balance and group_fully_busy and group_has_spare, migration kinds including migrate_load and migrate_util and migrate_task and migrate_misfit and migrate_llc_task, and locality values regular and remote and all. Numeric policy includes an overload scan cutoff near eighty five percent tied to imbalance_pct near one hundred seventeen, a minimal threshold NUMA_IMBALANCE_MIN, and failure patience offsets one and two beyond cache_nice_tries.
